terms.gloss: ancient, of the old Greeks and Romans
terms.comment: The Romans’ own word for what is old and venerable; the ancients, above all the ancient writers, are antīquī (Lewis & Short), and antiquity antīquitās. The classical languages are lingua Graeca et Latīna.
Gellius’s word for a first-rank author (see classic, an author), used in modern Latin of the classical age (aetās classica, Egger, in Morgan–Owens) and of classical music.
Also antīquitātēs Graecae et Rōmānae (Morgan–Owens). A classical scholar is an antīquārius (M-O s.v. classicist), classically one fond of antiquity (Tac. Dial. 21; Suet. Aug. 86, Lewis & Short).

sources: Lewis & Short: antiquus · Lewis & Short: antiquitas · Lewis & Short: classicus · Lewis & Short: antiquarius
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. classic, classical; classicist; classics.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 292.
